what_was_compared: Every PDF in the corpus manifests (corpus/*.lock.json), by SHA-256, read from the content store through corridor.storage.staged_file: each page's text as PyMuPDF's page.get_text() gave it before #740, against PDFium's textpage.get_text_range() (the replacement, read in a PdfiumExecutor process) and against pypdf's page.extract_text() (the alternative not chosen). Pages compare equal when corridor.verify.normalize (NFKC, line-break hyphens removed, punctuation and whitespace folded, case folded) of both texts is identical; that is the normalization literal_quote_on_page applies when it verifies a cited passage. token_multiset_equal counts pages whose normalized words are the same set in any order.
result: mismatch: the replacement reads differently from PyMuPDF on a large share of corpus pages; see summary and explained_differences
explained_differences: No permissive reader reproduces MuPDF's text assembly on customer PDFs. Sampled differences (matrix bcf988a9faed p.1, minutes e987872b10e0 p.1, agreement d7640245cd7f p.1): PDFium keeps the same words but orders table cells differently on drawn tables; pypdf merges or splits words at text-operator boundaries ('actionproposed', 'f ederal'); both readers include a word MuPDF omits on some minutes pages ('agenda'); scanned agreements carry OCR-layer punctuation that each reader spaces differently.

PDFium was chosen over pypdf for this call site because a cited passage must be a literal substring of the page text: PDFium's words are MuPDF's on 956 of 1246 pages (token multiset) against pypdf's 693, and pypdf's merged words would make short quotes unverifiable.

The reading is self-consistent: the model reads and the validator verifies the same _page_texts output, so a draft's retained passages remain literal quotes of what the person is shown. The draft registers nothing and preselects nothing; the confirmation reconstructs its binding from server-bound inputs (#362).
Three plan-set PDFs over 30 MB were not read in the comparison (documents_skipped_for_size).
